questions.question: Which of the following groups of animals produce ultrasound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dolphins, bats, and porpoises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ultrasound** is defined as sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper limit of human audibility, which is typically above **20,000 Hz** (20 kHz).
 
• **Bats** are well-known for producing ultrasonic squeaks. They use these high-frequency waves for **echolocation**, allowing them to navigate and hunt insects in total darkness by interpreting the echoes that bounce back from objects.
 
• **Dolphins** and **porpoises** produce ultrasonic clicks and whistles for underwater communication and **sonar**. These high-frequency sounds travel efficiently through water, helping them detect prey and obstacles with extreme precision.
 
• Certain other animals, such as **shrews** and some species of **moths**, also interact with ultrasound for survival, either by producing it for navigation or sensing it to avoid predators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classification of Sound Frequencies**:

 
 
• **Infrasound**: Sound waves with frequencies lower than **20 Hz**. These are produced by large animals like **elephants**, **rhinoceroses**, and **whales** (specifically baleen whales) to communicate over vast distances.
 
• **Audible Sound**: The frequency range that the human ear can perceive, spanning from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Ultrasound Applications**: In the medical field, **ultrasonography** uses high-frequency waves to visualize internal organs or fetal development. In industries, it is used for **ultrasonic cleaning** and detecting cracks in metal blocks.
 
 
 
• **Biological Variations**:
 
 
• While **dogs** can hear frequencies higher than humans (up to 45,000 Hz), they primarily communicate within the audible range and do not use ultrasound for navigation like bats or dolphins.
 
• **Moths** have developed the ability to hear the ultrasonic pulses of bats, which serves as an evolutionary defense mechanism to escape predation.

questions.question: A pencil partially dipped in water appears bent at the surface. Which phenomenon explains this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refraction** is the scientific phenomenon where light **changes direction** and **speed** as it passes from one transparent medium to another of different **optical density**.
 
• When a **pencil** is partially submerged in **water**, light rays reflecting from the underwater portion travel from water (an **optically denser medium**) into the air (an **optically rarer medium**).
 
• As these light rays cross the **interface** between water and air, they **speed up** and bend **away from the normal**.
 
• The human eye and brain trace these refracted rays back as **straight lines**, creating a **virtual image** of the pencil that appears at a shallower depth than its actual position.
 
• This displacement of the submerged part relative to the part in the air causes the pencil to appear **bent** or **broken** at the water surface.
 
• The degree of bending is determined by the **Refractive Index** of the materials, which for **water** is approximately **1.33** and for **air** is nearly **1.00**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reflection**

 
 
• Involves the **bouncing back** of light waves when they encounter a surface that does not absorb the energy.
 
• It follows the **Laws of Reflection**, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**
 
 
• Refers to the **bending of light** waves around the **edges** of an obstacle or through a narrow opening.
 
• It is most prominent when the size of the obstacle is comparable to the **wavelength** of the light.
 
 
 
• **Interference**
 
 
• Occurs when two or more light waves **superimpose** to form a resultant wave of greater, lower, or the same amplitude.
 
• This principle is responsible for the **iridescent colors** seen in thin films like soap bubbles or oil slicks.

questions.question: Which key fiscal reform was introduced in India after 1991 to strengthen revenue collection?

options.text: Introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simplifying indirect taxes through MODVAT**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Following the **1991 Economic Reforms**, India focused on **fiscal consolidation** to stabilize the economy and address the balance of payments crisis.
 
• The **Tax Reforms Committee (1991)**, chaired by **Dr. Raja J. Chelliah**, recommended structural changes to the tax system to improve efficiency and **revenue collection**.
 
• A major component of these reforms was the simplification of **indirect taxes** through the expansion of **MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax)**, which aimed to reduce the **cascading effect** of taxes (tax on tax).
 
• **MODVAT** allowed manufacturers to claim **input tax credit** for duties paid on raw materials and components, ensuring that tax was levied only on the **value added** at each stage of production.
 
• By streamlining the **excise duty** structure and reducing the multiplicity of rates, the government encouraged **tax compliance** and widened the tax base, leading to more robust revenue growth.
 
• Therefore, simplifying indirect taxes through MODVAT was a critical fiscal strategy introduced and expanded in the post-1991 era to strengthen the national treasury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**:

 
 
• While it is a landmark reform, it was officially implemented much later on **July 1, 2017**, under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• It integrated various indirect taxes like **Central Excise Duty**, **Service Tax**, and **State VAT** into a single unified tax.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Management Post-1991**:
 
 
• The government aimed to reduce the **fiscal deficit**, which had reached **8.4%** of GDP in **1990-91**.
 
• Reforms focused on **expenditure control**, meaning the policy was to rationalise or reduce **unproductive subsidies** rather than increase them.
 
• **Direct Tax Reforms** involved lowering **marginal tax rates** for individuals and corporations to discourage evasion and promote investment, rather than removing **income tax** entirely.

questions.question: What is a "slap shot" in hockey?

options.text: A shot taken with an open hand
A hard shot taken with a stick that is swung back and then quickly forward
A shot taken from a short distance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A hard shot taken with a stick that is swung back and then quickly forward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **slap shot** is a high-velocity technique in **ice hockey** designed to maximize power and speed, often reaching velocities over **100 miles per hour** (160 km/h).
 
• The execution involves three distinct phases: a **backswing** where the stick is raised above the waist or shoulder, a rapid **downswing**, and a follow-through.
 
• Scientifically, the player does not aim directly for the puck but strikes the **ice surface** roughly 1-2 inches behind it, causing the stick to **flex** significantly.
 
• This **mechanical flexing** stores **elastic potential energy** within the stick shaft, which is then released like a spring as the blade makes contact with the puck, propelling it forward with extreme force.
 
• The **slap shot** is statistically the most powerful shot in hockey but is generally considered less accurate than other shooting techniques due to the long delivery time and high force involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other technical shots:
 
 
• **Wrist Shot**: Unlike the slap shot, this technique involves the puck staying in contact with the blade throughout the motion. It relies on a quick **snap of the wrists** to generate **accuracy** and a **deceptive release**, making it the most common shot in **NHL** gameplay.
 
• **Snap Shot**: Often described as a hybrid, it uses a shorter backswing than a slap shot but still utilizes **stick flex** for power. It is prized for its ability to be released while the player is in full stride.
 
• **Historical Background**: **Bernard 'Boom Boom' Geoffrion** of the **Montreal Canadiens** is widely credited with innovating and popularizing the slap shot in the 1950s, while **Bobby Hull** later became famous for its terrifying speed.
 
• **Equipment Evolution**: The transition from **wooden sticks** to **carbon fiber composites** has allowed players to customize the **flex rating** of their equipment, further enhancing the power generated during a slap shot.

questions.question: Who assisted Humayun in regaining the Mughal throne after his exile?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Persian ruler Shah Tahmasp**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Following his decisive defeats against the **Afghan** ruler **Sher Shah Suri** at the **Battle of Chausa** (1539) and the **Battle of Kannauj** (1540), **Humayun** was forced to flee **India**.
 
• After years of wandering in **Sindh** and **Marwar**, **Humayun** sought political asylum in **Persia** at the court of the **Safavid** monarch, **Shah Tahmasp I**.
 
• **Shah Tahmasp** provided **Humayun** with a robust military force of approximately **12,000 cavalry** and **artillery** support to regain his lost territories.
 
• As a condition for this support, **Humayun** was required to adopt **Shia Islam** and agreed to cede the strategic territory of **Kandahar** to the **Persian** empire upon its conquest.
 
• With the backing of the **Safavid** army, **Humayun** first captured **Kandahar** and **Kabul** from his brother **Kamran Mirza** in **1545**, which eventually paved the way for his return to **Delhi** in **1555**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri**

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Suri Empire** and was responsible for ousting the **Mughals** from **India** for **15 years**.
 
• He is renowned for his administrative genius, including the introduction of the **Rupiya** and the restoration of the **Grand Trunk Road**.
 
 
 
• **Bahadur Shah of Gujarat**
 
 
• A powerful **Sultan** who expanded his kingdom into **Malwa** and **Rajasthan**.
 
• He was a constant threat to **Humayun** during the early **1530s** until his defeat and subsequent death in a conflict with the **Portuguese**.
 
 
 
• **Rana Sanga**
 
 
• The fierce **Rajput** ruler of **Mewar** who led a confederacy against **Humayun’s** father, **Babur**.
 
• He fought in the **Battle of Khanwa** in **1527** and died shortly thereafter in **1528**, well before **Humayun’s** exile.

questions.question: Where was India's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) set up?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India was a pioneer in **Asia** by recognizing the effectiveness of the **Export Processing Zone (EPZ)** model, leading to the establishment of the continent's first EPZ in **Kandla** in **1965**.
 
• The **Kandla Export Processing Zone (KASEZ)** was set up in the state of **Gujarat** near the **Gulf of Kutch** to leverage its strategic coastal location for international trade.
 
• The primary objectives of establishing the **EPZ** were to boost **industrialization**, promote **export-oriented production**, earn **foreign exchange**, and generate **employment opportunities**.
 
• Following the success of the **Kandla** model, several other **EPZs** were established across India, including **Santacruz** (Maharashtra), **Cochin** (Kerala), **Chennai** (Tamil Nadu), and **Noida** (Uttar Pradesh).
 
• In **2000**, the Indian government introduced the **Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Policy** to address the shortcomings of the **EPZ** framework, such as bureaucratic hurdles and lack of world-class infrastructure.
 
• By **2005**, the **SEZ Act** was enacted, and all existing **EPZs**, including **Kandla**, were converted into **Special Economic Zones** to provide a more competitive and investor-friendly environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mundra:**

 
 
• Located in the **Kutch district** of **Gujarat**, it is home to **India's largest private port** and a massive **multi-product SEZ** operated by the **Adani Group**.
 
• While it is a major economic hub today, it was developed much later than the **Kandla EPZ**.
 
 
 
• **Paradip:**
 
 
• Situated at the confluence of the **Mahanadi River** and the **Bay of Bengal** in **Odisha**, it is one of India's major **natural deep-water ports**.
 
• It primarily handles the export of **iron ore** and **coal** but was not the site of the first **EPZ**.
 
 
 
• **Haldia:**
 
 
• Located at the mouth of the **Hooghly River** in **West Bengal**, **Haldia Port** was developed as a **satellite port** to the **Kolkata Port**.
 
• It serves as a major **petrochemical** and **industrial hub** for Eastern India.

questions.question: Which ministry is associated with the inauguration of the Mahila Aarogyam Kaksh in July 2025?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Law and Justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Ministry of Law and Justice** spearheaded the inauguration of the **Mahila Aarogyam Kaksh**, a dedicated health and wellness facility established specifically for women within the **Judicial** ecosystem.
 
• The primary objective of this facility is to provide **gender-sensitive infrastructure**, offering **emergency medical care**, **primary health screenings**, and **first-aid** services to **women advocates**, **litigants**, and **court employees**.
 
• This initiative is part of a broader effort to modernize **judicial infrastructure** across **India**, ensuring that court complexes are inclusive and accommodate the specific health and hygiene needs of women.
 
• The **Mahila Aarogyam Kaksh** often functions in coordination with the **Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)** or **AIIMS** to ensure professional medical assistance is available during court working hours.
 
• By addressing the long-standing demand for medical rooms in court premises, the **Ministry of Law and Justice** aims to improve the working conditions for the increasing number of women entering the **legal profession**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Law and Justice:**

 
 
• It is the oldest limb of the **Government of India** and is responsible for the management of the **legal system**, **legislative drafting**, and **administration of justice**.
 
• The **Department of Justice** under this ministry focuses on the **e-Courts Mission Mode Project** and the **Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare:**
 
 
• Responsible for implementation of **national health programs** and oversees the **National Health Policy**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Women and Child Development:**
 
 
• Formulates policies and programs for the **empowerment of women** and the **protection of children**, such as **Mission Shakti**.

questions.question: As per Global Gender Gap Index 2025, India's performative score rose from 64.1% in 2024 to _____ in 2025.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**64.4%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Index** is an annual benchmark published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** that measures gender parity across **four key dimensions**.
 
• As per the **2025 Global Gender Gap Report**, India's performative score increased to **64.4%**, showing a marginal yet significant rise from its **2024** score of **64.1%**.
 
• The score represents the percentage of the **gender gap** that has been closed; a score of **100%** would indicate full gender parity, while **0%** would indicate full disparity.
 
• India's progress to **64.4%** reflects improvements in specific indicators such as **Educational Attainment** and certain aspects of **Political Empowerment**.
 
• The index benchmarks the progress of **146 countries** (as of recent cycles), providing a comprehensive overview of the status of women globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure of the Global Gender Gap Index**:

 
 
• **Economic Participation and Opportunity**: This sub-index includes indicators like **labor-force participation rate**, wage equality for similar work, and the ratio of women in **senior positions**.
 
• **Educational Attainment**: Measures the gap between women’s and men’s access to **primary, secondary, and tertiary education**, as well as literacy rates.
 
• **Health and Survival**: Focuses on the **sex ratio at birth** and the gap between women’s and men’s **healthy life expectancy**.
 
• **Political Empowerment**: Evaluates the ratio of women to men in **ministerial positions**, parliamentary seats, and the number of years with a **female head of state**.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF)**:
 
 
• An international non-governmental organization based in **Cologny, Switzerland**, founded in **1971** by **Klaus Schwab**.
 
• It is well-known for its annual meeting in **Davos** and for publishing high-impact reports like the **Global Risks Report** and the **Global Competitiveness Report**.

questions.question: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution is related with which of the following?

options.text: Validation of certain Acts and Regulations.
Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**, which allows citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed under **Part III**.
 
• Dr. **B.R. Ambedkar** described this article as the **'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'** because it makes the fundamental rights functional and enforceable.
 
• Under this article, the **Supreme Court** acts as the **guarantor** and **defender** of fundamental rights and has the power to issue directions or orders.
 
• The court can issue five types of **Prerogative Writs**: **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, **Prohibition**, **Certiorari**, and **Quo-Warranto**.
 
• This right cannot be suspended except as otherwise provided for by the **Constitution** (such as during a **National Emergency** under **Article 359**).
 
• The **Supreme Court** has ruled that **Article 32** is a **Basic Structure** of the Constitution, implying it cannot be removed even via a constitutional amendment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Validation of certain Acts and Regulations**:

 
 
• This relates to **Article 31B**, which was added by the **1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951**, to protect laws included in the **Ninth Schedule** from judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Freedom to manage religious affairs**:
 
 
• This is a fundamental right guaranteed under **Article 26**, allowing religious denominations to manage their own affairs in matters of religion and own property.
 
 
 
• **Protection of interests of minorities**:
 
 
• This is covered under **Article 29**, which grants any section of citizens residing in India the right to conserve their distinct **language, script, or culture**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Article 226**:
 
 
• While **Article 32** gives powers to the **Supreme Court**, **Article 226** empowers **High Courts** to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following article of Indian constitution deals with the courts not to inquire into proceedings of the Legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 212**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 212** of the **Indian Constitution** specifically restricts the **Judiciary** from inquiring into the internal proceedings of the **State Legislature**.
 
• According to **Article 212(1)**, the validity of any proceedings in the **Legislature of a State** cannot be called into question in any court on the ground of any alleged **irregularity of procedure**.
 
• **Article 212(2)** provides that no **officer** or **member** of the Legislature in whom powers are vested for regulating **procedure**, conducting **business**, or maintaining **order** shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court regarding the exercise of those powers.
 
• This article is a cornerstone of the **Separation of Powers** doctrine in India, designed to protect the **independence** and **sovereignty** of the legislative branch from judicial overreach.
 
• It ensures that the **House** remains the sole master of its own **internal proceedings**, facilitating the smooth functioning of democracy without constant legal interruptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 213**:

 
 
• Relates to the **Legislative power** of the **Governor**, specifically the authority to promulgate **Ordinances** when the **State Legislature** is not in session and urgent action is required.
 
 
 
• **Article 211**:
 
 
• Imposes a **restriction on discussion** within the State Legislature, prohibiting members from discussing the **conduct of any Judge** of the **Supreme Court** or a **High Court** while they are discharging their duties.
 
 
 
• **Article 208**:
 
 
• Deals with the **Rules of Procedure**, granting each House of the **State Legislature** the power to frame rules for regulating its **procedure** and the **conduct of its business**.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms originated in Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest and most widely recognized **classical dance** forms of India, having originated in the southern state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The dance form traces its roots back to the **Sadir Natyam**, a solo dance performed by temple dancers known as **Devadasis** in ancient South Indian temples.
 
• It is theoretically grounded in the **Natya Shastra**, an exhaustive ancient Sanskrit treatise on performing arts attributed to **Sage Bharata**, dating between **200 BCE** and **200 CE**.
 
• The performance is characterized by distinct movements like the **Aramandi** (half-squat position), intricate footwork, and a complex system of **Mudras** (hand gestures) used for storytelling.
 
• A traditional performance follows a specific sequence: **Alarippu** (invocation), **Jatiswaram** (pure dance), **Shabdam** (short compositions), **Varnam** (the centerpiece), **Padam** (expressive lyrics), and **Tillana** (concluding rhythmic piece).
 
• The dance is accompanied by **Carnatic music**, typically featuring instruments like the **Mridangam**, **Nadeswaram**, **Flute**, and **Cymbals** handled by the **Nattuvanar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thiruvathirakali**:

 
 
• This is a popular **folk dance** performed by women in the state of **Kerala** during the festival of **Onam** and **Thiruvathira**.
 
• It is performed in a circular motion around a **Nilavilakku** (ceremonial lamp) to signify unity and devotion.
 
 
 
• **Bagurumba**:
 
 
• This is a traditional folk dance of the **Bodo tribe** in the state of **Assam**, often referred to as the butterfly dance.
 
• The dancers wear colorful traditional attire like the **Dokhona** and **Aronai**, mimicking the movements of nature.
 
 
 
• **Veeranatyam**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Dance of the Brave**, it is a ritualistic folk dance from **Andhra Pradesh** associated with the **Veerabhadra** cult.
 
• The performance is highly energetic and is usually conducted in **Shiva** temples using huge percussion instruments.

questions.question: The traditional dance 'Seecha and Kukui Kucho' belongs to which of the following regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seecha** and **Kukui Kucho** are indigenous traditional folk dances performed by the **Angami Naga** tribe, which is one of the major ethnic groups in the state of **Nagaland**.
 
• These dance forms are primarily showcased during the **Sekrenyi** festival, a ten-day celebration observed in **February** that signifies purification and the sanctification of the community.
 
• The **Seecha** dance is characterized by synchronized movements and rhythmic chanting, traditionally performed by men in full **warrior attire** to depict bravery and historical triumphs.
 
• **Kukui Kucho** is a communal dance that reflects the agricultural lifestyle and social bond of the **Angami** people, often accompanied by the melodious tunes of indigenous instruments like the **Tati**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagaland**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **Land of Festivals**, it is home to **16 major tribes**, each possessing distinct customs, languages, and traditional dances.
 
• The **Hornbill Festival**, held in the first week of **December** at **Kisama Heritage Village**, is a major cultural event where all tribes perform their traditional dances, including the **War Dance** and the **Zeliang** bamboo dance.
 
• Other notable folk dances from the state include **Monyu Asho** (Phom tribe), **Melo Phita** (Angami tribe), and **Aaluyattu** (Konyak tribe).
 
• The **Sekrenyi** festival, where **Seecha** is performed, involves rituals like **Phousanyi** (cleansing) and the **Thekra Hie** (folk singing by the youth).

questions.question: The acronym "NCMRWF" is associated with union ministry of Indian government?

options.text: Ministry of Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Earth Sciences**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NCMRWF** stands for the **National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting**, which is a premier scientific institution specializing in **Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP)** and computational atmospheric science.
 
• It functions as a subordinate office under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)**, Government of India.
 
• Originally established in **1988** under the **Department of Science and Technology**, it was later integrated into the newly created **Ministry of Earth Sciences** in **July 2006**.
 
• Located in **Noida, Uttar Pradesh**, the center is mandated to develop and provide high-resolution **Global and Regional** forecast models to improve the prediction accuracy of the **Indian Summer Monsoon**.
 
• It utilizes state-of-the-art **High-Performance Computing (HPC)** infrastructure, such as the **Mihir supercomputer**, to generate **medium-range forecasts** that cover a period of **3 to 10 days**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)**:

 
 
• It was formed in **2006** to provide a holistic approach to **oceanography**, **meteorology**, **hydrology**, and **seismology**.
 
• Other key bodies under this ministry include the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, **Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM)**, and **INCOIS**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**:
 
 
• Responsible for planning and coordinating **environmental and forestry policies**, including **wildlife conservation** and the **National Action Plan on Climate Change**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Cooperation**:
 
 
• Created in **July 2021**, this ministry focuses on strengthening the **cooperative movement** in India under the vision of **'Sahakar se Samriddhi'**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Education**:
 
 
• Formerly known as the **Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD)**, it oversees **School Education**, **Higher Education**, and the implementation of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.

questions.question: 'Silnyen' or 'Bubjal', used in Ladakh, are types of which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cymbals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silnyen** and **Bubjal** (often spelled **Bugjal** or **Bup-chal**) are traditional percussion instruments essential to the cultural and religious fabric of **Ladakh** and the broader **Trans-Himalayan** region.
 
• Both instruments are classified as **idiophones**, specifically types of **cymbals** made from **brass**, **bronze**, or other metallic alloys to produce resonant sounds.
 
• **Silnyen** is a flat, rimless cymbal typically used in **Tibetan Buddhist** monastic rituals to accompany melodic chants and provide a subtle rhythmic pulse.
 
• **Bubjal** is characterized by a large, prominent central **boss** or dome; these cymbals are struck together horizontally to produce a loud, clashing sound used to drive the rhythm of **Cham dances** (sacred masked dances).
 
• These instruments are rarely played in isolation and are usually part of a monastic ensemble that includes drums and long horns to facilitate **meditation** and **tantric ceremonies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ladakhi Musical Instruments:
 
 
• **Surna**: A double-reed wind instrument, similar to the **Shehnai**, which provides the melody in traditional Ladakhi folk and festival music.
 
• **Daman**: A set of two kettle drums made of copper and covered with leather, traditionally played by the **Mon** community.
 
• **Lingbu**: A traditional **flute** used by shepherds and in folk songs across the high-altitude plateaus.
 
• **Dhyangro**: A frame drum used primarily by **shamans** and in specific ritualistic contexts in the Himalayan belt.
 
 
 
• Monastic Context:
 
 
• In **Gompas** (monasteries), musical instruments represent **sensory offerings** to deities, where the **Silnyen** represents peaceful sound and the **Bubjal** represents wrathful or powerful sound.
 
• The **Dungchen** (long copper horn) and **Gyaling** (oboe-like instrument) are often paired with these cymbals during major festivals like **Hemis Tsechu**.

questions.question: Which mission of NASA will explore Jupiter's moon Europa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Europa Clipper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Europa Clipper** is a major **NASA** interplanetary mission specifically designed to study **Europa**, one of **Jupiter's** most intriguing Galilean moons.
 
• Launched on **October 14, 2024**, aboard a **SpaceX Falcon Heavy** rocket, the spacecraft aims to determine if there are places below the moon's icy surface that could support life.
 
• The mission does not orbit the moon itself but instead orbits **Jupiter**, performing **49 close flybys** of Europa to protect the sensitive electronics from the planet's intense **radiation belts**.
 
• Key scientific goals include measuring the thickness of the **ice shell**, investigating the interaction between the **subsurface ocean** and the surface, and characterizing the **geological features** of the moon.
 
• The spacecraft is the largest ever built by **NASA** for a planetary mission, featuring massive **solar arrays** to harvest sunlight in the dim environment of the outer solar system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **JUICE (Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer)**:

 
 
• This is a mission led by the **European Space Agency (ESA)**, launched in **April 2023**.
 
• While it will fly past Europa and Callisto, its primary objective is to eventually enter orbit around **Ganymede**, making it the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than Earth's moon.
 
 
 
• **Europa's Habitability**:
 
 
• Europa is considered a primary target for **astrobiology** because it likely harbors a **salty liquid water ocean** containing more water than all of Earth's oceans combined.
 
• The mission carries **nine science instruments**, including **ice-penetrating radar** (REASON) and a **magnetometer**, to confirm the ocean's depth and salinity.
 
 
 
• **Legacy Missions**:
 
 
• The **Galileo spacecraft** (1989–2003) provided the initial data suggesting the existence of Europa's ocean, which inspired the development of the **Europa Clipper** mission.

questions.question: _____ can also be observed when a fine beam of light enters a room through a small hole.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tyndall effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tyndall effect** is defined as the phenomenon where a beam of light is scattered by **colloidal particles** or particles in a very fine suspension, making the path of the light visible to the observer.
 
• When a fine beam of light enters a dark room through a small hole, it is intercepted by **dust and smoke particles** suspended in the air. These particles scatter the incident light in various directions, which allows the trajectory of the beam to be clearly seen.
 
• The intensity of the scattered light depends on the **density of the particles** and the **frequency** of the incident light. Generally, shorter wavelengths (blue light) are scattered more strongly than longer wavelengths (red light).
 
• This effect can also be observed in nature when sunlight passes through the **canopy of a dense forest**. In this scenario, the **mist** contains tiny droplets of water that act as colloidal particles dispersed in the air, causing the light to scatter.
 
• The Tyndall effect is used to distinguish between a **true solution** and a **colloidal solution**, as true solutions do not scatter light because their particles are too small (usually less than 1 nanometer).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brownian movement**

 
 
• It describes the continuous, **random zig-zag motion** of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas).
 
• This motion results from the constant **bombardment** of the particles by the fast-moving molecules of the surrounding medium.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**
 
 
• It refers to the **bending of light waves** as they pass around the edge of an object or through a narrow aperture.
 
• This phenomenon is most prominent when the size of the obstacle or opening is comparable to the **wavelength** of the light.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion**
 
 
• It is the process where **white light** splits into its seven constituent colors (VIBGYOR) when it passes through a transparent medium like a **glass prism**.
 
• This occurs because different colors of light travel at different speeds through the medium, resulting in different degrees of **refraction**.

questions.question: The Khelo India Winter Games 2024 is the ___ edition of the annual event in the Khelo India calendar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khelo India Winter Games 2024** represented the **fourth edition** of the prestigious national-level multi-sport event specifically dedicated to winter sports in India.
 
• The 2024 event was divided into two legs; the first leg was hosted in **Leh, Ladakh** from **February 2 to 6**, and the second leg took place in **Gulmarg, Jammu and Kashmir** from **February 21 to 25**.
 
• A total of **six major sports** disciplines were featured in this edition, including **Ice Hockey**, **Ice Skating**, **Ski Mountaineering**, **Alpine Skiing**, **Snowboarding**, and **Nordic Skiing**.
 
• The **Indian Army** emerged as the overall champion of the **4th edition**, securing the top spot in the medal tally with a total of **21 medals**, including **10 gold medals**.
 
• The event serves as a critical component of the broader **Khelo India** program, aimed at identifying grass-root level talent and preparing athletes for the **Winter Olympics** and other international arenas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mascot and Cultural Significance**:

 
 
• The official mascot for the **2024 games** was **Sheen-e She**, a **Snow Leopard**. This choice was made to highlight the ecological importance of the **Himalayan region** and the conservation of the endangered snow leopard species.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Games**:
 
 
• The **1st edition** was inaugurated in **2020** with venues in both **Leh** and **Gulmarg**, marking the beginning of organized national winter sports competitions.
 
• The **2nd edition** followed in **2021**, primarily hosted in **Gulmarg**, showcasing increased participation from various states and union territories.
 
• The **3rd edition** was held in **2023** in **Gulmarg**, where the Union Territory of **Jammu and Kashmir** topped the medal table.
 
 
 
• **Governance**:
 
 
• The games are organized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** in coordination with the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** and the **Winter Games Association** of the respective host regions.
